title: Config perturbation matrices and explainable regression alerts for batching & cache
creator: Asha Raman
description: Goal: Build a repeatable experiment and alerting pattern that ties small configuration perturbations for batching and KV-prefix caching to explainable quality regressions and latency improvements. We need to move beyond binary regression flags: produce a ranked matrix of config perturbations, an explainability layer that attributes quality delta to specific knobs, and an alerting policy suitable for canary rollouts. This ticket covers the experiment harness, metric definitions, visualizations, and an initial monitoring/playbook integration.
background: We frequently tweak microbatch sizes, ttl/eviction settings for KV cache, and cache scope (per-route vs global). Some changes produce subtle quality regressions on rare slices while improving median latency. Existing regression alerts are noisy and give limited actionability. We need a structured perturbation matrix + attributions to (1) identify safe operating points on the latency-quality frontier, (2) point engineers to which knob or workload slice drove a regression, and (3) automate conservative rollbacks during canary deployments.
proposed_experiment_matrix: Generate orthogonal perturbation matrices across these axes: microbatch_size (1,2,4,8), kv_ttl_seconds (0,30,300,3600), cache_scope (route, model, tenant), prefix_merge (on, off), microbatch_accumulation_window_ms (5,10,20). For each cell run N=3 seeds of the same prompt sample and collect token-level latencies, model outputs, and KV hit/miss traces. Use paired comparisons vs baseline config.
steps: 1) Implement perturbation runner in runtime-ci to spin up controlled inference jobs and capture traces
2) Instrument extra signals: per-token kv_hit, kv_eviction_event, microbatch_fill_fraction, kernel_selection_tag
3) Run full matrix on a representative 2k prompt sample -> collect outputs and latencies
4) Compute pairwise deltas vs baseline and derive a latency-quality frontier (Pareto curve) for each model/config-family
5) Apply SHAP-inspired attribution on feature-perturbation space to score which knobs most correlate with quality regressions
6) Surface top-3 config causes per regression in Grafana and in the rollout decision log
7) Add automated canary policy: if regression_attribution_score > 0.6 for high-severity slices and semantic_similarity_delta < -0.02 then block rollout and trigger rollback playbook
acceptance_criteria: Perturbation runner can execute full matrix and ingest results into eval-store
Pipeline produces a latency-quality frontier visualization for a given model and dataset
For any detected regression, system provides top-3 config attributions and supporting evidence (example prompts with diffs)
Grafana dashboard with gullwing frontier + slice breakdown exists and is linked from the rollout UI
Canary rollout policy callable: automated rollback trigger works in staging and is covered by integration tests
monitoring_playbook: Alert types: (A) Delta-alert: semantic_similarity_delta <= -0.02 for slices labeled 'core-ux' -> Pager; (B) Attribution-alert: regression_attribution_score > 0.6 with kv_ttl or microbatch_size as top contributor -> Slack #runtime-alerts with recommended mitigations; (C) Latency-tail-regression-only -> Info channel. Recommended mitigations: revert to previous config, tighten TTL or reduce microbatch size, or narrow cache_scope. Include an automated canary rollback hook that uses the attribution score + slice severity to decide immediate rollback.
rollout_plan: Test in canary1 (internal) for 48h with synthetic high-sensitivity slice traffic; if no high-severity regression alerts, promote to canary2 (limited production: 5% traffic) for 24h. During both canaries, run the full perturbation matrix jobs nightly and compare. If attribution alerts fire, block promotion and open postmortem ticket. Document decision in rollout log.
expected_outcomes: A reproducible matrix that maps config cells to delta metrics
Reduced false-positive regression noise by 30% via attribution filtering
Faster root cause identification: time-to-owner decreased from hours to <30 minutes for config-driven regressions
Actionable Grafana + Rollout automation integrated into runtime canary flow
notes: This work should be coordinated with Observability (for dashboard ownership) and Product (for slice definitions). Keep experiments deterministic where possible: fix RNG seeds, snapshot model versions and tokenizer commits. Watch out for confounding changes (model weights, tokenization updates) during runs. Consider synthetic amplification of rare slices if production traffic is too sparse.
